content:
We are asked to find the number $N$ of positive integer divisors of $17017^{17}$ that are congruent to $5$ modulo $12$, and then compute $N \bmod 1000$.

First factor $17017$:
\[
17017 = 7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 17.
\]
Hence
\[
17017^{17} = 7^{17} \cdot 11^{17} \cdot 13^{17} \cdot 17^{17}.
\]
Every divisor $d$ can be written uniquely as
\[
d = 7^{a} \cdot 11^{b} \cdot 13^{c} \cdot 17^{e}
\]
with $a,b,c,e \in \{0,1,\dots,17\}$.

We need $d \equiv 5 \pmod{12}$. Since $\gcd(7,12)=\gcd(11,12)=\gcd(13,12)=\gcd(17,12)=1$, we can reduce each factor modulo $12$ and multiply the residues.

Compute the residues of the prime powers modulo $12$:

- $7 \equiv 7$. Because $7^2 = 49 \equiv 1 \pmod{12}$, we have
  \[
  7^{a} \equiv \begin{cases}
  1 & \text{if } a \text{ is even},\\
  7 & \text{if } a \text{ is odd}.
  \end{cases}
  \]

- $11 \equiv 11 \equiv -1 \pmod{12}$. Hence
  \[
  11^{b} \equiv \begin{cases}
  1 & \text{if } b \text{ is even},\\
  11 & \text{if } b \text{ is odd}.
  \end{cases}
  \]

- $13 \equiv 1 \pmod{12}$, so $13^{c} \equiv 1$ for all $c$.

- $17 \equiv 5 \pmod{12}$. Since $5^2=25\equiv 1 \pmod{12}$, we have
  \[
  17^{e} \equiv \begin{cases}
  1 & \text{if } e \text{ is even},\\
  5 & \text{if } e \text{ is odd}.
  \end{cases}
  \]

Let $A$ denote the residue of $7^{a}$, $B$ the residue of $11^{b}$, and $D$ the residue of $17^{e}$. Then $d \equiv A \cdot B \cdot D \pmod{12}$. The condition $d \equiv 5 \pmod{12}$ becomes
\[
A \cdot B \cdot D \equiv 5 \pmod{12}.
\]

We have $A \in \{1,7\}$, $B \in \{1,11\}$, $D \in \{1,5\}$. Check all $8$ combinations:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
A & B & D & A\cdot B\cdot D \bmod{12} \\ \hline
1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\
1 & 1 & 5 & 5 \\
1 & 11 & 1 & 11 \\
1 & 11 & 5 & 11\cdot5=55\equiv 7 \\
7 & 1 & 1 & 7 \\
7 & 1 & 5 & 7\cdot5=35\equiv 11 \\
7 & 11 & 1 & 77\equiv 5 \\
7 & 11 & 5 & 7\cdot11\cdot5=385\equiv 1 \\
\end{array}
\]

Only two combinations yield $5$:
\[
(A,B,D) = (1,1,5) \quad\text{and}\quad (7,11,1).
\]

Translating back to parity conditions on the exponents:

- $(1,1,5)$ corresponds to $a$ even, $b$ even, $e$ odd.
- $(7,11,1)$ corresponds to $a$ odd, $b$ odd, $e$ even.

Now count the number of exponent choices $(a,b,e)$ satisfying these parity conditions.

The possible exponents are $0,1,\dots,17$ — $18$ values each. Exactly half are even and half odd because $18$ is even:
- even $a$: $0,2,\dots,16$ → $9$ choices.
- odd $a$: $1,3,\dots,17$ → $9$ choices.
Similarly for $b$ and $e$.

Thus:
- For case 1 ($a$ even, $b$ even, $e$ odd): $9 \times 9 \times 9 = 729$ triples.
- For case 2 ($a$ odd, $b$ odd, $e$ even): $9 \times 9 \times 9 = 729$ triples.

Total number of valid $(a,b,e)$ triples: $729+729 = 1458$.

The exponent $c$ for the factor $13$ can be any value from $0$ to $17$ inclusive, and it does not affect the residue condition because $13^{c} \equiv 1 \pmod{12}$. Hence there are $18$ choices for $c$.

Therefore the total number of divisors satisfying the condition is
\[
N = 1458 \times 18 = 26244.
\]

Finally, we need $N \bmod 1000$. Compute:
\[
26244 \div 1000 = 26 \text{ remainder } 244.
\]
Thus the remainder is $244$.

\[
\boxed{244}
\]
